P14.1 (T4): Intrinsic raw-transform image beyond the known regimes
For a pseudoeﬀective class α on a compact Kähler manifold, intrinsically characterize the im-
age of the perturbation-independent raw ideal-valuative DXZ transform on the MP spectrum.
The full Kähler image and the projective ample rational-line-bundle regime are established.
The big non-nef image remains open; the full real Néron–Severi DXZ–BJ comparison does not
assert the same literal ideal formula outside the rational-line-bundle case.

Construct a positivity theory for big non-nef classes retaining P -singularity data, movable-
positive-part data, or equally informative additional structure. A relatively nef total-space
model cannot represent a non-nef generic class. The raw ideal-valuative transform is only
I-level data and cannot by itself distinguish P -types or recover raw mass.

P14.5 (T5): Monge–Ampère measures in the big non-nef realization
Construct the Monge–Ampère measure theory corresponding to a valid big non-nef, P -
sensitive realization, with the correct mass and comparison with existing positive-volume
DXZ and MP operators in their common scopes.

P14.6 (T5): Energy in the big non-nef realization
Construct the corresponding intrinsic energy theory and its continuity, diﬀerentiation and
measure compatibility. State which additional singularity data and reference choices it needs;
positive-volume I-level energy alone does not supply a P -sensitive theory.

P14.8 (T5): Zero-mass and formal-data reconstruction
Go beyond the established realizable-I-data dichotomy: formulate and solve arbitrary formal-
data realization, a general all-semivaluation reconstruction formula, or the remaining zero-
mass strict-interior reconstruction range with precise admissibility conditions. A canonical
normalized I-model can be recovered from realizable data, but raw representatives and raw
mass cannot descend to the I-quotient. The terminal DXZ left-limit result does not create a
second zero-mass interval.

 e_m(\psi_{m,D})=C_{m,D}^{n+1}/(n+1)-cV_m\to E(P_\theta(f_D)),
 \quad p_{m*}\MA_{A_m,\rm raw}(\psi_{m,D})\to\mu_D.
 \tag{5.4}
\]
The last limit pairs (5.1) with each fixed vertical Cartier test, then
uses model density and the converging raw masses. Finite nef model
measures have coefficient $b_E(C_{m,D}|_E)^n$ by G0's finite ample
perturbation, with the model fixed through that polynomial limit.
The divisibility-increasing full section stages have the envelope as
their supremum on $U$ by Lemma~\ref{density}. A cleared Kodaira section
times a generating ample system makes a cofinal tail finite on $U$.
The decreasing G1 multiplier-ideal stages are finite there too: their
base ideals contain the corresponding full-system base ideals, and their
additional fixed model weight is bounded. Thus the same endpoint on $U$
is both a supremum and an infimum of finite continuous functions; it is
finite continuous. Compact positive-gap superlevels now give the net
Dini argument. It proves compact-uniform convergence of $q_{T_m}$ to $R$
and of the quotient to $P_\theta(f_D)-R$.
Their generic values tend to $P_\theta(f_D)(v_0)$ by the same section
minorants at $v_0$. This is zero for the normalized envelopes used in
the subsequent zero-generic-error limits. A general nonpositive obstacle
need not have normalized envelope; its finite stages are shifted by the
same actual constant when normalization is required.

For fixed $m$, a bounded nonpositive relatively generated scalar $\psi$
on $A_m$, and a fixed original continuous $f\geq q_{T_m}+\psi$,
multiply by the actual $s_{\ell T_m}$ to inject the full auxiliary

the original infimum. All other original weights are at least
$\ell\min f$. Extend an adapted subspace basis to the full filtered

are bounded by the ranks. This proves
\[
 \mathscr E(f)\geq e_m(\psi)+(\min_K f)(V-V_m).
 \tag{5.5}
\]
The last, generally negative, term is retained until $m\to\infty$ at

\section{Finite Hodge estimates and genuine contraction}
On a smooth SNC total model with $F=\sum_i b_iE_i$, relatively nef
slots $\Gamma=N_1\cdots N_{n-1}$, and $D=\sum_i b_i a_iE_i$,
\[
 -D^2\Gamma=\sum_{i<j}b_ib_j(E_iE_j\Gamma)(a_i-a_j)^2\geq0.
 \tag{6.1}
\]
This follows from the zero row identities
$\sum_j b_j(E_iE_j\Gamma)=0$ and positivity on each SNC stratum.
Resolve $|f_D|$ by principalizing
$\OO(-q(CF+D))+\OO(-q(CF-D))$ after clearing denominators.
Its normalized coefficients are exactly $|a_i|$ on the refined model.
The inequality $||a_i|-|a_j||\leq|a_i-a_j|$ and projection formula
prove contraction of the quadratic form under absolute value; the same
proof works for rational piecewise linear one-Lipschitz functions.

On an actual generated nef $A$, put $T_\xi=(A,\xi)$,
$e_A(\xi)=T_\xi^{n+1}/(n+1)$, $J_A(\xi)=V_A\xi(v_0)-e_A(\xi)$.
For $S=(0,\xi-\eta)$ the correct finite tangent formula is
\[
 T_\eta^{n+1}-T_\xi^{n+1}+(n+1)ST_\eta^n
 =-\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(n-j)S^2T_\xi^jT_\eta^{n-1-j}.
 \tag{6.2}
\]
Expanding two telescoping sums gives the multiplicity $n-j$.
Let $d_A(\xi,\eta)$ be the maximum of these $n$ quadratic forms.
Then $J_A(\xi)$ is their weighted sum relative to zero divided by
$n+1$, and hence is comparable to $d_A(\xi,0)$ with dimension constants.
The midpoint defect $\delta_A$ satisfies
\[
 \frac{n}{4^{n+1}}d_A(\xi,\eta)\leq\delta_A(\xi,\eta)
 \leq\frac n8 d_A(\xi,\eta).
 \tag{6.3}
\]
For $p(t)=e_A(\eta+t(\xi-\eta))$, $-p''$ is $n$ times the positive
Bernstein combination of those forms. Integrate against
$\min(t,1-t)/2$. Its integral is $1/8$; on $[1/4,3/4]$ the kernel
and each Bernstein monomial give the stated lower coefficient.

The finite slot-change calculation uses only (6.1), Cauchy--Schwarz and
(6.2). For completeness set $\tau=(\xi+\eta)/2$, $f=\xi-\eta$,
$a=d_A(\xi,\eta)$, $b=\max(d_A(\xi,\rho),d_A(\eta,\rho))$,
$b_j=\|f\|^2_{T_\rho^jT_\tau^{n-1-j}}$.
The average expansion gives $b_0\asymp_n a$, while the seminorm
triangle inequality gives $b_{n-1}\leq4b$. Replacing one slot gives
$b_{j+1}-b_j=-S^2(0,\rho-\tau)T_\rho^jT_\tau^{n-2-j}$.
Write one $S=T_\xi-T_\eta$ and apply Cauchy--Schwarz separately in
the two nef forms. Since each $T_\xi,T_\eta$ is bounded by $2T_\tau$
in positive quadratic forms, this is at most $C_n\sqrt{b_jb}$.
Here quasi-convexity of $d_A$ follows from the convex tangent remainder
in (6.2). If $a\leq b$, induction gives
$b_j\leq C_n a^{2^{-j}}b^{1-2^{-j}}$; if $a>b$, use $b_{n-1}\leq4b$.
Applying this to differences through a third potential gives the
dimension-only quasi-triangle inequality. Average a finite desired list
of slots; its expanded power dominates each mixed positive quadratic
form. With $\beta=2^{1-n}$ this proves
\[
 \|\xi-\eta\|^2_{T_{\rho_1}\cdots T_{\rho_{n-1}}}
 \leq C_n d_A(\xi,\eta)^\beta
       \max(J_A(\xi),J_A(\eta),J_A(\rho_l))^{1-\beta}.
 \tag{6.4}
\]
This reconstructs the primary finite calculation with the corrected
tangent orientation. It imports no unbounded ample estimate.

Resolving $g=|\xi-\eta|$, telescope from the trivial measure
$V_A\delta_{v_0}$ to $\MA_A(\zeta)$, starting at $j=0$.
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz, absolute contraction and (6.4) in each term.
Put $\alpha=2^{-n}$ and let $B_*$ be the maximum of the three costs
$J_A(\xi)$, $J_A(\eta)$ and $J_A(\zeta)$. Then
\[
 \int|\xi-\eta|d\MA_A(\zeta)
 \leq V_A|\xi(v_0)-\eta(v_0)|
   +C_n\delta_A(\xi,\eta)^\alpha J_A(\zeta)^{1/2}B_*^{1/2-\alpha}.
 \tag{6.5}
\]
All multiplicities and raw volumes are present. For $n=1$ omit the
last exponent-zero factor. Zero-volume cases follow from positivity and
mass; no division by $V_A$ occurs.

For $\psi\leq0$ set
$a_k=\int(-\psi)\MA_A(\psi^{[k]},0^{[n-k]})\geq0$.
The finite energy identity gives $-e_A(\psi)=(n+1)^{-1}\sum a_k$,
and $a_0=-V_A\psi(v_0)$. Expanding the finite nef polynomial gives
\[
 -e_A(r\psi)\leq r a_0+2^{n+1}r^2(-e_A(\psi)),\quad0\leq r\leq1.
 \tag{6.6}
\]
The terms with $k=0$ sum to at most $ra_0$; every other term has
another factor $r$, with total binomial coefficient bounded by $2^{n+1}$.
For $u=P_\theta(f_D)$ use the actual physical minorant
$q_{T_m}+r\psi_{m,D}\leq(1-r)R+ru$ in (5.5). Hold each continuous
majorant fixed, then take $m\to\infty$ in (5.4), retaining the vanishing
generic term and the missing-volume term, then take the outer infimum.
This proves the genuine contraction
\[
 B((1-r)R+ru)\leq2^{n+1}r^2B(u),\qquad B(u)=-E(u).
 \tag{6.7}
\]
Canonical model envelopes and decreasing energy continuity prove it for
every normalized actual $u\in\EE$. Rational $r$ extends to real $r$
by concavity and continuity along its genuine finite-energy segment.

For every normalized genuine $q$, the truncations
$q_j=\max(q,R-16^j)$ have cost at most $V16^j$.
Put $a_j=(1-8^{-j})R+8^{-j}q_j$ and
$p_m=\sum_{j\leq m}2^{-j}a_j+2^{-m}R$.
Contraction and concavity bound its cost by $2^{n+1}V/7$.
It decreases genuinely with generic value zero, so closure and decreasing
energy continuity give $p\in\EE$. Where $q=-\infty$ and $R$ is finite,
$R-p_m=m$. Thus this one actual E1 pole covers the pole of $q$ outside
the reference poles. In particular applying it to $W$ from (2.2)
constructs the required genuine finite-energy $Z$-pole.

\section{The original outer derivative and signed big margin}
For $f_D\leq0$, $\mathscr E(f_D)\geq-B$ and $c>B/V$, put
$g_D(c)=\vol(\rho_X^*L+D+cF)/(n+1)$.
Formula (4.2) makes $g_D$ convex, $V$-Lipschitz, zero at $c=0$ and
eventually $cV+\mathscr E(f_D)$, with $g_D(c)\geq cV-B>0$.
Thus the deficient class is genuinely big. Its positive derivative
measure $\mu_{D,c}$ has mass between $V-B/c$ and $V$.
There is coefficientwise domination
\[
 0\leq\mu_{D,c}\leq\mu_D,
 \quad\|\mu_D-\mu_{D,c}\|_{\rm TV}\leq B/c.
 \tag{7.1}
\]
Indeed the actual full-lattice trace
$\mathscr E(f_D)+cV-g_D(c)
=\lim n!m^{-n-1}\sum_j\min(w_{mj}+mc,0)$ is monotone under
adding any effective vertical divisor: inclusion of the full filtration
raises each ordered weight. Differentiate this monotonicity in each
effective $E$. The difference coefficient is nonnegative. Convexity
in $c$ gives its stated mass bound.

Fix one rational original model test $h=f_H$ on a fixed determination.
Choose ample $T$ there, $\gamma=\rho_X^*L+cF$, and
$\kappa=(n+1)(cV-B)>0$, $M=(n+1)\langle\gamma^n\rangle T$.
For every refinement carrying $D$, volume loss along $\alpha-rT$
while big is at most $rM$, since $\alpha=\rho_X^*L+D+cF\leq\gamma$.
Boundary continuity excludes a first exit before
$r_0=\kappa/[2(M+1)]$. Choose $a$ with $aT\pm H$ nef and put
$\lambda=a/r_0$. Then $\lambda\alpha\pm H$ are psef, so for
$|s|\lambda<1/2$ positive-product order sandwiches
$\langle(\alpha+sH)^n\rangle$ between
$(1\pm\lambda|s|)^n\langle\alpha^n\rangle$.
Pair separately with the two fixed nef terms $aT+H$ and $aT$.
This bounds the derivative variation uniformly over all $D$ and refinements
and gives a fixed $K_c$ quadratic remainder for $g_{D+tH}(c)$.

For the full energy use the nonpositive obstacle
$f_D+sh-|s|H_0$, $H_0=\|h\|_\infty$, and parameter
$c_s=c+|s|H_0$. Its cost is at most $B_s=B+2V|s|H_0$.
Impose, before differentiating either sign,
\[
 |t|H_0<(c-B/V)/2,\qquad |t|<1.
 \tag{7.2}
\]
Then $c_s>B_s/V$ throughout the path, whose actual deficient class is
exactly $\alpha+sH$. The rough bound $B+2VH_0$ by itself does not
prove this when $c$ is just above $B/V$. Integrate the positive derivative
tail (7.1) and restore the subtracted scalar. The result is
\[
 |\mathscr E(f_D+th)-\mathscr E(f_D)-t\mu_D(h)|
 \leq K_ct^2/2+|t|H_0(2B+2VH_0)/c.
 \tag{7.3}
\]
All order estimates use fixed nef tests. Both signed perturbations have
the verified margin (7.2).

For $u\in\EE$ use its canonical nonpositive model majorants $f_i$.
Their positive mass-$V$ measures have weak cluster points on original
compact $K$. At fixed $t$, their perturbed genuine envelopes decrease
exactly to $P_\theta(u+th)$, with decreasing energies. Pass the whole
increment (7.3) along a cluster, then divide with each sign, let $t\to0$
at fixed $c$, and finally $c\to\infty$. It gives a unique cluster $M(u)$
and
\[
 \left.\frac d{dt}\right|_0E(P_\theta(u+th))=\int h\,dM(u).
 \tag{7.4}
\]
Uniform model approximation changes each divided increment and integral
by at most $V$ times its sup error. Thus (7.4) holds for every original
continuous $h$. This is a target-independent outer-energy map, positive
of raw mass $V$, on actual functions on $K$.
The envelope and energy constant laws show directly from (7.4) that
$M(u+c)=M(u)$ for every real $c$; no target equation is used for this.
For ordered bounded-cost endpoints $a\geq b$, compare their perturbed
energy increments with (7.3); for fixed model $h$,
\[
 |M(a)(h)-M(b)(h)|\leq (E(a)-E(b))/t+K_ct+C_{h,B}/c.
 \tag{7.5}
\]
This proves decreasing weak continuity. At $u=P_\theta(f_D)$ apply
it to model majorants and their minima with $f_D$: the latter have
exactly the same envelope and energy as $f_D$. First (7.5) makes their
derivatives equal to $\mu_D$, then compares them to the canonical
majorants. Thus $M(P_\theta(f_D))=\mu_D$.

For an actual effective Cartier $S$, the vertical divisor moment of
$\mu_{D,c}$ is bounded by
$\langle\alpha_D(c)^n\rangle\rho_X^*S$; its effective horizontal
part has nonnegative volume derivative. A fixed nef upper test gives
one $C_{S,c}$ independent of $D$. For the original continuous caps
$b_N=\min(v(S),N)$, (7.1) implies
\[
 \int b_N\,dM(u)\leq C_{S,c}+NB/c.
 \tag{7.6}
\]
Divide by $N$, take $N\to\infty$, then $c\to\infty$.
Hence $M(u)(S^{\rm an})=0$, in particular $M(u)(Z)=0$.
This argument gives algebraic nullness and uniform algebraic collars.
It does not yet identify all unbounded genuine weighted products.

\section{Intrinsic targets and what pre-attainment estimates supply}
For a positive original Radon measure $\nu$ of raw mass $V$, missing
$\{R=-\infty\}$, set
\[
 I_\nu(u)=\int(R-u)d\nu,\qquad
 D_\nu=\sup_{u\in\EE,\ u(v_0)=0}\{I_\nu(u)-B(u)\}.
 \tag{8.1}
\]
The difference is taken where $R$ is finite; no absolute integrability
of $R$ is stipulated. Finite $D_\nu$ implies integrability of every
genuine relative E1 test directly. Conversely if all are integrable,
their integrals are uniformly bounded on $B(u)\leq1$: otherwise choose
$I_\nu(u_j)\geq4^j$ and take the genuine decreasing convex sums
$\sum_{j\leq m}2^{-j}u_j+2^{-m}R$ of bounded cost. Their actual E1
endpoint has infinite relative integral by ordinary countable monotone
convergence. Contraction (6.7), with $r=(2^{n+1}B(u))^{-1/2}$ for
large cost, then bounds $I_\nu(u)$ by a constant times $1+\sqrt{B(u)}$,
so $D_\nu<\infty$. Thus (8.1) is an intrinsic relative energy condition.
It implies $\nu(Z)=0$ using the actual E1 pole constructed above.

Writing $C_0=2^{n+1}$, contraction also gives
\[
 I_\nu(u)\leq\epsilon B(u)+C_0D_\nu/\epsilon,
 \qquad 0<\epsilon\leq C_0.
 \tag{8.2}
\]
Hence near-maximizers have bounded actual energy cost. Section density
on $U$ and directed continuous Radon integration show that model-envelope
objectives have exactly the same supremum. The Radon net assertion used
here is elementary: increasing continuous superlevels on $U$ cover each
compact subset of the limiting open superlevel by finitely many sets;
directedness gives one dominating index, inner regularity gives its mass,
and finite layer-cake sums give the integral. No measurable-net monotone
convergence assertion is imported.

Choose model near-maximizers $a_j$ within $\varepsilon_j\to0$ and bounded
cost. Their outputs are finite divisorial measures. For a fixed continuous
test $h$, $z_{j,t}=P_\theta(a_j+th)$ lies between
$a_j\pm|t|\|h\|$. Its objective and obstacle inequality give
$E(z_{j,t})-E(a_j)-t\nu(h)\leq\varepsilon_j$.
Both signs of the uniform fixed-increment bound (7.3), first at fixed
$c,t$, then $j\to\infty$, then $t\downarrow0$, then $c\to\infty$,
prove $M(a_j)\to\nu$ weakly. This uses no attained inverse.

For fixed model envelopes $a,b,w$, (5.5) applied to every fixed majorant
of $(a+b)/2$ gives
$\limsup_m\delta_{A_m}(\psi_{m,a},\psi_{m,b})\leq\delta(a,b)$,
where $\delta(a,b)=E((a+b)/2)-(E(a)+E(b))/2$.
This is only an upper midpoint estimate; it does not assume the bounded
barycenter identification proved later. Formula (6.5), compact-uniform
bounded quotient convergence on $U$, and weak endpoint output convergence
then give the absolute model estimate. On a fixed continuous cutoff in
$U$, bounded changing tests pass by uniform convergence; omitted mass
is bounded by the limiting measure's omitted mass, since it misses $Z$.
Canonical output approximation and increasing continuous relative costs
extend it to all genuine tests and outputs:
\[
 \int|a-b|dM(w)\leq
 C_n\delta(a,b)^\alpha B(w)^{1/2}
       \max(B(a),B(b),B(w))^{1/2-\alpha}.
 \tag{8.3}
\]
First use $a=R$, bounded majorants of $b$, and the bound
$\delta(R,b_i)\leq B(b)/2$ to prove every actual relative test
integrable at $M(w)$. Then pass two test nets separately in absolute
$L^1$; their midpoint energies decrease. The same model-pair passage
through the pre-attainment outputs $M(a_j)\to\nu$ gives (8.3) at a
target, with the output cost bound of that sequence. These arguments
retain all generic terms in (6.5) before the degree limit.

Every output consequently satisfies the intrinsic target condition.
For fixed relative tests, (8.3) bounds the ordered majorant errors
uniformly over any bounded-cost output family. Fixed bounded relative
tests pass weak convergence on a fixed $U$ cutoff; then those absolute
errors pass the unbounded test. Contact is already forced by (4.7): at
$a=P_\theta(f_D)$ the equality $E(a)=\mathscr E(f_D)$ and $a\leq f_D$
give $0\leq\int(a-f_D)d\mu_D\leq0$. Thus finite planes, these exact
contact integrals, and the fixed-test passage give the whole supporting plane
\[
 E(v)\leq E(u)+\int(v-u)dM(u),\qquad u,v\in\EE.
 \tag{8.4}
\]
This is an outer-map plane, not the entire mixed-operator identification.

\section{Exact quotient traces and bounded physical identification}
Fix an actual $p:Y\to X$ with $p^*L=A+T$, $A$ nef and generated in
cleared degree, $T\geq0$. Multiplication by $s_{\ell T}$ injects the
\emph{full} $H^0(Y,\ell A)$ as a fixed subspace $S_\ell$ of
$R_\ell=H^0(X,\ell L)$. Let $V_A=A^n$, $\varepsilon=V-V_A\geq0$.
Use the induced subspace and quotient flags of the original (4.5) flag.
Extend an adapted subspace basis to a full adapted basis. Its trace is
exactly the sum of subspace and quotient traces. Uniform shifts by
$\ell\|f-g\|$ also shift every ordered quotient weight by at most this
amount. Quotient rank asymptotics therefore give
\[
 |\mathscr Q_A(f)-\mathscr Q_A(g)|\leq\varepsilon\|f-g\|,
 \qquad\mathscr Q_A=\mathscr E-\mathscr H_A.
 \tag{9.1}
\]
The same finite flag argument gives monotonicity. Rounding error is at
most the quotient rank and vanishes in the trace scaling.

Here is the required actual restricted-lattice calculation. Take a smooth
common equivariant total determination \emph{mapping to}
$Y\times\mathbb P^1$ and carrying the original obstacle $f_D$.
Write the total pulled $T$ as $T^{\rm hor}+T^{\rm ver}$. A generic
section in the restricted space has the literal form $s_{\ell T}a$,
$a\in H^0(Y,\ell A)$. In an actual local frame, its original extension
order is the order of $a$ plus the order of $s_{\ell T}$ in the pulled
frame. Along every central prime this is the extension condition in
\[
 p^*L+D-T^{\rm hor}=p^*A+D+T^{\rm ver}.
 \tag{9.2}
\]
Along horizontal primes, regularity as a section of the latter bundle
is precisely regularity of $a$ as a section of $A$ on its fixed generic
model. Thus both implications hold at every prime: multiplying gives
the original section with the prescribed horizontal zeros; division
gives an actual $A$ section and the retained central orders.
Normality identifies sections with these orders. Consequently this is
the full relative lattice of (9.2), not a selected series. Its retained
vertical term is exactly the one used in the corrected complete moving
formula (5.2), before its effective residual base divisor is removed. This argument
requires the actual morphism to the specified auxiliary product; it
does not replace it by numerical equality. The example of blowing up
$(z,t)=(0,0)$ on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ has
$p_X^*\{z=0\}=T^{\rm hor}+E$; the vertical $E$ term in (9.2)
is essential, and its cancellation confirms rather than contradicts
the formula.

If $V_A>0$, the time-twisted bundle (9.2) is big for sufficiently
large $c$. Its full lattice diagonalizes, and (4.2)--(4.4) applied to
this actual bundle give the restricted intercept $\mathscr H_A(f)$,
and its positive finite divisorial derivative $\mu_{A,T;f}$ of mass
$V_A$. Original and restricted derivatives test the same pulled original
model direction. The derivative of (9.1) has norm at most $\varepsilon$
and value $\varepsilon$ on the constant one, by the two constant laws.
A real functional with these properties is positive: for $0\leq h\leq1$,
the norm bound on $1-h$ gives its value on $h$ at least zero.
Model density extends this to continuous tests. Hence
\[
 0\leq\mu_f-p_*\mu_{A,T;f},\qquad
 \|\mu_f-p_*\mu_{A,T;f}\|_{\rm TV}=V-V_A.
 \tag{9.3}
\]
If $V_A=0$, restricted rank is $o(\ell^n)$ and its fixed-obstacle
weights are bounded linearly in $\ell$, so its trace and derivative
are zero directly. No differential at a nonbig class is used. In the
moving setting a cofinal tail has $V_m>0$ by (5.4).

Suppose a bounded rational generated scalar $-C\leq\xi_m\leq0$
on $A_m$ has actual physical FS stage $v_m=q_{T_m}+\xi_m$, and
$f\geq v_m$ is an original model obstacle with $f(v_0)\leq0$.
All full restricted weights lie in $[-\ell C,0]$: the lower bound
uses $f\geq v_m$ and the canonical norms of auxiliary sections, and
the upper bound evaluates at $v_0$. Taking powers of the rational
weighted generators of $\xi_m$, after clearing their weights, shows
that the complete restricted stages $\sigma_{\ell,f}$ satisfy
$\xi_m\leq\sigma_{\ell,f}\leq0$ and
$\sigma_{\ell,f}\leq f-q_{T_m}$ at function-field divisorial points.
The fixed twist $c>C+1$ makes each compactified complete system
globally generated. Its full section bundle is the fixed big class
$\beta=p^*A_m+D+T_m^{\rm ver}+cF$.
Complete-base-system Fujita gives its nef moving top volumes tending
to $\vol(\beta)$. Subtracting the fiber term proves
\[
 e_m(\sigma_{\ell,f})\to\mathscr H_{A_m}(f).
 \tag{9.4}
\]

Volume convergence identifies every fixed derivative test as well.
Let $\Gamma_\ell\leq\beta$ be these complete nef models. They satisfy
$\Gamma_\ell\leq p^*L+cF$. For a fixed original model direction $H$,
choose a fixed globally nef big $\omega$ above this last class with
$\omega\pm H$ nef, on a fixed determination carrying $H$, and pull
it to the common refinements. The numerical upper bound suffices for
BFJ Corollary 3.4; the actual effective difference $\beta-\Gamma_\ell$
also gives volume order. For both signs of $t$ the independently read
Morse bound gives
\[
 \vol(\beta+tH)\geq\Gamma_\ell^{n+1}
             +(n+1)t\Gamma_\ell^nH-Kt^2.
 \tag{9.5}
\]
The same $K$ works for all $\ell$. Pass top volumes first; the positive
and negative signs bound limsup and liminf of $\Gamma_\ell^nH$.
Then let $t\to0$. BFJ differentiability gives
$\Gamma_\ell^nH\to\langle\beta^n\rangle H$.
For vertical tests this is exactly the finite restricted derivative.
Model density and its fixed raw mass therefore identify the weak limit
of its finite top measures with $\mu_{A_m,T_m;f}$. This proves the
complete two-sided derivative squeeze, without an unbounded auxiliary
operator or uniform Fujita rate across changing obstacles.

Finite concavity at $\xi_m$ and (9.4) give, with
$\sigma_m=\MA_{A_m,\rm raw}(\xi_m)$,
\[
 0\leq\mathscr H_{A_m}(f)-e_m(\xi_m)
 \leq\int\min(C,f-v_m)d\sigma_m.
 \tag{9.6}
\]
For a fixed original test $h$, ordered finite energy telescoping gives
$I\leq(n+1)$ times the ordered gap. A fixed-$C$ twist makes all
bounded auxiliary bundles nef and dominated by $p^*L+cF$.
Writing $H$ as two fixed nef tests bounds its quadratic forms in these
slots, independently of $m,f$ and refinements. Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 |p_*\mu_{A_m,T_m;f}(h)-p_*\sigma_m(h)|
 \leq C_{h,C}\sqrt{\mathscr H_{A_m}(f)-e_m(\xi_m)}.
 \tag{9.7}
\]
The constant is fixed before the moving limit.
The same fixed twist bounds $\int v(S)d\sigma_m$ uniformly for
every fixed effective original divisor $S$: its vertical part is the
finite moment, its horizontal part is effective, and a fixed nef test
bounds the total intersection by a positive product of $p^*L+cF$.
Thus auxiliary collar masses are at most $C_{S,c}/H$.
Original bounded-cost outputs have the separate collar bound
$C_{S,c}/H+D/c$ from (7.6). Both collars must be kept distinct.

\begin{theorem}[Actual bounded generated quotient identification]\label{bounded}
Let $w\in\EE$ be normalized, continuous on $U$ and
$R-C\leq w\leq R$. Suppose $-C\leq\xi_m\leq0$ are rational
generated quotients on the common complete-system $A_m$, their generic
values tend to zero, their actual original FS stages $v_m$ are at most
$w$ on all lifts, and $\xi_m\to w-R$ uniformly on each compact subset
of $U$. Then $e_m(\xi_m)\to E(w)$ and $p_*\sigma_m\to M(w)$ weakly.

degree with nonempty complete system. Resolve its base ideal once:
\[
 p_m^*L=A_m+T_m,\qquad mA_m\text{ generated},\quad mT_m\geq0.
\]
Fix a smooth equivariant model carrying a rational vertical divisor $D$
over $X\times\mathbb P^1$. On a common smooth determination mapping
to the actual generic product $X_m\times\mathbb P^1$, write
\[
 \rho^*T_m=T_m^{\rm hor}+T_m^{\rm ver}.

\]

second is supported over zero. Both are actual divisors; they are not
interchangeable numerical representatives. Let $F$ be the full fiber.

to that common determination.

\begin{theorem}[Retained vertical fixed part]\label{verticalformula}
Divide the sections in (2) by the canonical section of
$mT_m^{\rm hor}$, and let $G_{m,D}^{\rm ver}\geq0$ be the
resolved residual base divisor. The actual complete moving bundle is
\[
 C_{m,D}=\rho^*A_m+D+T_m^{\rm ver}+cF
                       -m^{-1}G_{m,D}^{\rm ver}.          \tag{3}
\]
It is globally generated in degree $m$, and hence nef. Its generic
bundle is $A_m$. The bounded auxiliary quotient scalar is the model
scalar represented by $D+T_m^{\rm ver}-m^{-1}G_{m,D}^{\rm ver}$.

original stage satisfies $\phi_{m,D}=q_{T_m}+\psi_{m,D}$.

Multiplication by the fixed section identifies
$H^0(X_m,mA_m)$ with $H^0(X,mL)$: every original section is divisible by
the prescribed common generic base-divisor factor, and normal proper
birational descent identifies the remaining spaces. Every section of
(2) therefore vanishes along $mT_m^{\rm hor}$. This gives an actual
division of regular sections and puts the residual sections in
\[

   =m(\rho^*A_m+D+T_m^{\rm ver}+cF).                      \tag{4}
\]

are present and the original generic moving system is complete and
generated. At infinity the endpoint monomials also recover the entire
generic generated system. Consequently the residual base ideal is
supported at zero. Principalization makes it the invertible ideal of
the effective vertical $G_{m,D}^{\rm ver}$. Removing that ideal gives
(3), generated by the same full list of sections. It removes every
fixed component of the entire absolute system, exactly once.

weighted maximum gives the actual bounded generated scalar on $A_m$.

divisor factor is finite, and gives the same literal $-\infty$ value

exactly the one in (3) minus its fiber twist. Thus the scalar and actual
bundle identifications agree, without subtracting infinite values.

\begin{abstract}
We construct a smooth projective surface with a big non-nef real class
and two positive-mass potentials having the same multiplier ideals at
every real scale, the same first-degree nonpluripolar current, and the
same nonpluripolar Monge--Amp\`ere measure, but different normalized

mass ranging over $[0,2]$. Thus even adjoining the raw mass, or the
nonpluripolar products on this fixed surface, to the ideal data does
not retain $P$-equivalence. The construction uses explicit diffuse
polar measures, with elementary proofs of polarity and exponential
integrability. This is a partial analytic obstruction to a proposed
data signature, not a non-Archimedean realization or a solution of

\section{Definitions, imports, and exact scope}
Our convention is
\[
 \ddc=\frac{i}{2\pi}\partial\bar\partial,
 \qquad \ddc\log|z|^2=\delta_0.
\]
For a smooth real closed $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ on a compact K\"ahler
manifold, $\PSH(X,\theta)$ consists of functions $u$, not identically
$-\infty$, such that $u+\rho$ is plurisubharmonic on each sufficiently
small coordinate open set with a smooth local potential
$\ddc\rho=\theta$. We use the canonical upper semicontinuous psh
representatives. In particular $u$ is locally integrable and
$T_u=\theta+\ddc u\geq0$. Upper semicontinuity and this distributional
inequality alone do not define the admissible class: an upward change
at one point can preserve them while violating the psh submean inequality.
All rooftop competitors below use the stated local psh condition.
The multiplier ideal is
\[
 \calI(cu)_x=\{f\in\mathcal O_{X,x}: |f|^2e^{-cu}
                \text{ is locally integrable}\},\qquad c>0.
\]
We write $\langle T_u^k\rangle$ for the nonpluripolar product and
$M_\theta(u)=\int_X\langle T_u^n\rangle$ for the raw mass. There is
no probability normalization in this paper.

The normalized singularity envelope is
\[
 P_\theta[u]=\left(\lim_{C\to+\infty}
 P_\theta(u+C,0)\right)^*,\qquad
 P_\theta(f,g)=\left(\sup\{v\in\PSH(X,\theta):
                               v\leq\min(f,g)\}\right)^*.
\]
The star denotes upper semicontinuous regularization. For the
positive-mass potentials used here, $P$-equivalence means equality
of these envelopes in the fixed background $\theta$. Our ideal data
are the actual family $(\calI(cu))_{c>0}$; equality of these data is
stronger than merely assuming a particular asymptotic formula.

Here are all the essential imported analytic results.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Nonpluripolar construction.}
For local psh potentials $u_1,\ldots,u_k$, the product is the increasing
limit of
\[
 {\bf1}_{\bigcap_j\{u_j>-N\}}
 \ddc\max(u_1,-N)\wedge\cdots\wedge\ddc\max(u_k,-N).
\]
It puts no mass on pluripolar sets; when well defined it depends only
on the currents and is local in the plurifine topology. For closed
positive $(1,1)$-currents on a compact K\"ahler manifold it is well
defined. These are \cite[\S1.2, Definition 1.1, Propositions 1.4 and
1.6]{BEGZ}. We only need ordinary locality on open sets where the
current is smooth, and the noncharging property. We never truncate
a global $\theta$-psh potential by a constant while assuming that
the result remains $\theta$-psh for a nonpositive $\theta$.
\item \textbf{Unrestricted mass monotonicity.}
Let $X$ be compact K\"ahler, let $\theta_j$ be smooth closed real
$(1,1)$-forms, and let $u_j,v_j\in\PSH(X,\theta_j)$, $1\leq j\leq n$.
If each $u_j$ is less singular than $v_j$, meaning $v_j\leq u_j+C_j$,
then
\[
 \int_X\left\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^n
                   (\theta_j+\ddc u_j)\right\rangle
 \geq
 \int_X\left\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^n
                   (\theta_j+\ddc v_j)\right\rangle.
\]
This is \cite[Theorem 1.1]{DDL}. In particular, bounded difference
implies equality of top masses. No small-unbounded-locus assumption
is imposed in this theorem.
\item \textbf{Positive-mass envelope theorem.}
Assume $\{\theta\}$ is big, $\phi\in\PSH(X,\theta)$, $\phi\leq0$,
and $M_\theta(\phi)>0$. Define
\[
 F_\phi=\{v\in\PSH(X,\theta):
               \phi\leq v\leq0,
               M_\theta(v)=M_\theta(\phi)\}.
\]
Then $P_\theta[\phi]\in F_\phi$ and
$P_\theta[\phi]=\sup_{v\in F_\phi}v$; in particular it is idempotent.
This is the assertion of \cite[\S3.2, the paragraph preceding
Lemma 3.7, and Theorem 3.12]{DDL}. We use only
\[
                 \phi\leq P_\theta[\phi]\leq0,
          \qquad M_\theta(P_\theta[\phi])=M_\theta(\phi).
\]
We apply it only to strictly positive masses, never to the zero-mass
endpoint of our family.
\end{enumerate}
The source of \cite{DDL} writes its Hessian as $i\partial\bar\partial$.
To apply it with our convention, replace its potentials by $u/(2\pi)$,
keep the smooth forms $\theta$ fixed, and rescale envelope obstacles
and constants by the same positive factor. The positive currents,
orders of singularity, and their masses are then identical. This is
a change of convention, not an assertion about non-Archimedean norm

\section{The analytic statement}
Let $Y=\Pone_z\times\Pone_w$ and normalize the Fubini--Study forms
$\omega_z,\omega_w$ to have integral $1$ on their respective factors.
We use the same symbols for their pullbacks to $Y$. Set
$\beta=\omega_z+\omega_w$, let $p=(\infty,\infty)$, and let
\[
 \pi:X=\operatorname{Bl}_pY\longrightarrow Y
\]
be the blowup, with exceptional divisor $E$. Write $H=\pi^*\{\beta\}$.
Fix $a>0$, choose a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $\mathcal O_X(E)$,
let $\rho=c_1(\mathcal O_X(E),h)$, and put
\[
 e=\log|\sigma_E|_h^2,\qquad
 \theta=\pi^*\beta+a\rho,\qquad
 \alpha=H+a\{E\}.
\]
Scale $h$ so that $e\leq0$. Poincar\'e--Lelong gives
$\ddc e=[E]-\rho$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
The class $\alpha$ is big and non-nef on the smooth connected compact
K\"ahler surface $X$. There are functions $U_0,U_1\in\PSH(\Pone,\omega_z)$,
each nonpositive and smooth outside a compact polar set, such that,
for $j=0,1$ and $0<s\leq1$,
\[
 \Phi_{j,s}=ae+sU_j\circ\operatorname{pr}_z\circ\pi
                    \in\PSH(X,\theta),\qquad \Phi_0=ae,
\]
have the following properties. At $s=0$ the notation means $\Phi_0$;
no product $0(-\infty)$ is used.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every real $c>0$,
\[
 \calI(c\Phi_{j,s})=\calI(c\Phi_0)
                   =\mathcal O_X(-\lfloor ca\rfloor E).
\]
Consequently for every semivaluation $v$ of coherent ideals centered
on $X$, including those with nontrivial support,
\[
 \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m v(\calI(m\Phi_{j,s}))
                  =a\,v(\mathcal I_E).
\]
\item Define the smooth semipositive form
\[
 S_s=(1-s)\pi^*\omega_z+\pi^*\omega_w,
             \qquad S_0=\pi^*\beta.
\]
Then for $k=1,2$,
\[
 \langle T_{\Phi_{j,s}}^k\rangle=S_s^k,
 \quad \MA_\theta(\Phi_{j,s})
       =2(1-s)\pi^*(\omega_z\wedge\omega_w),
 \quad M_\theta(\Phi_{j,s})=2(1-s).
\]
These formulas also hold for $\Phi_0$ at $s=0$.
\item For every $0<s<1$,
\[
                     P_\theta[\Phi_{0,s}]
                       \ne P_\theta[\Phi_{1,s}].
\]
Thus the entire ideal family together with both nonpluripolar
products on $X$ does not determine the $P$-envelope, even at a fixed
strictly positive raw mass.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\section{Explicit diffuse polar measures}
Put $\ell_0=1$ and $\ell_n=\exp(-4^n)$ for $n\geq1$. Start with
$[0,1]$. Inside each level-$n$ interval retain the two closed
level-$(n+1)$ intervals of length $\ell_{n+1}$ at its endpoints.
The children are disjoint because $2\ell_{n+1}<\ell_n$; for $n=0$
this follows from $2e^{-4}<1$, and for $n\geq1$ from
$\log2<3\cdot4^n$. Let $C$ be the intersection of the retained
unions. Bernoulli measure on binary choices gives a probability
$\mu_0$ on $C$ whose mass on each level-$n$ interval is $2^{-n}$.
Nested lengths tend to zero, so this construction defines a Borel
probability and $\mu_0(\{x\})\leq2^{-n}$ for every $n$: it is atomless.
Let $D=C+2$ and let $\mu_1$ be the translate of $\mu_0$ to $D$.
The sets $C,D$ are disjoint and avoid $\infty$.

For finite $t$, the spherical Green kernel is
\[
 G_t(z)=\log\frac{|z-t|^2}{(1+|z|^2)(1+|t|^2)},
 \quad G_t\leq0,\quad \ddc G_t=\delta_t-\omega_z.
\]
It extends in the usual affine coordinate at infinity. Define
\[
                         U_j(z)=\int G_t(z)\,d\mu_j(t).
\]

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:green}
The function $U_j$ is upper semicontinuous and locally integrable,
$\ddc U_j=\mu_j-\omega_z$, and it is smooth and finite off
$\operatorname{supp}\mu_j$. It equals $-\infty$ at every point of
that support. For every $b>0$, $e^{-bU_j}$ is locally integrable.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The logarithmic kernel has uniformly bounded local $L^1$ norm when
$t$ lies in a compact interval. Fubini therefore proves local
integrability of the integral and justifies the displayed distributional
Hessian identity. Since $G_t\leq0$, Fatou's lemma applied to $-G_t$
proves upper semicontinuity. Local integration of the psh kernels
$\log|z-t|^2$, plus the smooth term, or the submean inequality
integrated in $t$, identifies this representative as quasi-psh.
Off the compact support, the kernel and every derivative are uniformly
bounded on smaller neighborhoods, proving smoothness there. In
particular the function is not identically $-\infty$.

If $x\in C$, let $I_n$ be its level-$n$ interval. Since $G_t(x)\leq0$
everywhere and $G_t(x)\leq2\log\ell_n$ for $t\in I_n$,
\[
 U_0(x)\leq 2^{-n}\,2\log\ell_n=-2\cdot2^n\longrightarrow-\infty.
\]
The identical estimate applies on $D$ to $U_1$. Thus the pole sets
are exactly $C$ and $D$, and are polar by the existence of these
nontrivial local subharmonic potentials. Their planar Lebesgue
measure is zero: the total interval length at level $n$ is
$2^n e^{-4^n}\to0$.

For exponential integrability, the assertion is immediate off the
support. Near $z_0$ on it, choose a disc $B(z_0,r)$ of measure
$\delta<1/b$, possible because the measure has no atom at $z_0$.
On a smaller disc $B(z_0,r/2)$ the potential of the complementary
measure and the smooth spherical terms are bounded. If $\delta=0$
there is nothing to prove. Otherwise normalize the restricted measure

\[

\]

\[
 \int_{|w|<2r}|w|^{-2b\delta}\,dA(w)
 =2\pi\frac{(2r)^{2-2b\delta}}{2-2b\delta}<\infty.
\]

\section{Geometry, positivity, and ideals}
\begin{proof}[Proof of bigness and non-nefness]
The blowup is smooth and projective. For completeness, it also has
an explicit ample class $A=2H-\{E\}$. Embed $Y$ in $\mathbf P^3$
by $\mathcal O_Y(1,1)$. The three hyperplanes through $p$ generate
the ideal of $p$ after this twist: away from $p$ at least one is
nonzero, and at $p$ their restrictions generate the maximal ideal,
since the embedding separates tangent directions. The blowup is
the closure of the graph of the resulting projection to $\mathbf P^2$,
and embeds in $Y\times\mathbf P^2$, hence in
$\mathbf P^3\times\mathbf P^2$. Its two hyperplane pullbacks have
classes $H$ and $H-\{E\}$. The Segre embedding restricts to a projective
embedding of $X$ with hyperplane class $A=2H-\{E\}$. Let $\kappa_A$
be the induced Fubini--Study K\"ahler form. Then
\[
 \alpha=\tfrac12 A+(a+\tfrac12)\{E\}
\]
contains the K\"ahler current
$\tfrac12\kappa_A+(a+\tfrac12)[E]$, proving bigness. This also
exhibits a compact K\"ahler structure on $X$.

The exceptional normal bundle is $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(-1)$,
so $E^2=-1$. Pullbacks from $Y$ have zero intersection with $E$,
and $H^2=\int_Y\beta^2=2$. Thus
$\alpha\cdot E=-a<0$. A nef class has nonnegative degree on every
compact curve, by restriction of K\"ahler approximants, so $\alpha$
is not nef. Notice that $\alpha^2=2-a^2$, which is not the formula
for the raw masses below.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of positivity and Theorem \ref{thm:main}(1)]
Write $q=\operatorname{pr}_z\circ\pi$. By Lemma \ref{lem:green},
\[
 \beta+\ddc(sU_j\circ\operatorname{pr}_z)
  =(1-s)\omega_z+s\operatorname{pr}_z^*\mu_j+\omega_w\geq0.
\]
The functions are smooth near $p$, since their supports avoid
$\infty$. Their pullbacks are therefore smooth near $E$. Away from
$E$, $\pi$ is an isomorphism; pulling local psh potentials back
there proves positivity. This defines the positive current on all
of $X$ without any unsupported rule for pulling back a Hessian
equation through an arbitrary map. Poincar\'e--Lelong gives
\[
 T_{\Phi_{j,s}}
   =a[E]+\pi^*\big((1-s)\omega_z
                  +s\operatorname{pr}_z^*\mu_j+\omega_w\big)\geq0.
\]
The potentials are locally integrable and nontrivial, so are
$\theta$-psh.

Away from $E$, the term $ae$ is smooth; the possible singularities
there come from $sU_j(z)$. Lemma
\ref{lem:green} with $b=cs$, and Fubini in the $w$ coordinate,
give integrability of $e^{-c\Phi_{j,s}}$. Every holomorphic germ is
bounded on a smaller coordinate neighborhood, hence the multiplier
ideal is the unit ideal there. At $E$, in a local defining coordinate
$\zeta$, the function is $a\log|\zeta|^2+O(1)$, independently of $j,s$.
The multiplier ideal is therefore $(\zeta^{\lfloor ca\rfloor})$:
\[
 \int_0^\varepsilon r^{2k-2ca+1}\,dr<\infty
                    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad k+1>ca.
\]
The least allowed integer $k$ is $\lfloor ca\rfloor$, including when
$ca$ is integral. For a holomorphic germ not divisible by this power,
its first nonzero coefficient in the $\zeta$-expansion is nonzero on
an open set of the other coordinate; Fubini then proves divergence.
This checks necessity for arbitrary germs, not just monomials. These
local descriptions glue to the asserted global sheaf.

Put $w=v(\mathcal I_E)$. If $w<\infty$, the value of the $m$th
ideal is $\lfloor ma\rfloor w$ and division by $m$ converges to $aw$.
If $w=+\infty$, then $\lfloor ma\rfloor>0$ for all sufficiently large
$m$, so all those ideal values are $+\infty$ and the limit is
$+\infty$. The unit ideal has value zero even at a supported
semivaluation; no expression $0\cdot\infty$ is used. This proves
the formula at every semivaluation without a density argument.
\end{proof}

\section{Nonpluripolar products and the same-mass separation}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:main}(2)]
For $j=0,1$, set
\[
 Z_j=E\cup q^{-1}(\operatorname{supp}\mu_j).
\]
It is pluripolar: $E$ is locally a logarithmic pole, and the other
set is a pole set of the pulled back quasi-psh function, which is
nontrivial on every local chart. Alternatively, for $s>0$ it is the
pole set of the already constructed $\Phi_{j,s}$. On the ordinary
open complement of $Z_j$, all the functions are smooth, the measure

\[

applies to $\Phi_0$ at $s=0$.

Since the square of a form pulled back from a curve is zero,
\[
 S_s^2=2(1-s)\pi^*(\omega_z\wedge\omega_w).
\]
The latter smooth volume form has integral $1$, because $\pi$
is an isomorphism outside $E$ and $\{p\}$ and these sets have zero
volume. Its coefficient therefore gives mass $2(1-s)$, including
the zero measure at $s=1$. We did not take a limit of Monge--Amp\`ere
measures at a singular endpoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:main}(3)]
Fix $0<s<1$ and abbreviate $\phi_j=\Phi_{j,s}$. The function
$\max(U_0,U_1)$ is bounded on $\Pone$. It is at most zero; near
each of the two disjoint compact supports the other function is

\[

into a maximum of two psh functions. On $E$, both terms are

\[

Suppose the two normalized envelopes were equal to $P$. The
positive-mass envelope theorem applies, since $\alpha$ is big,

\[

Thus $W\leq P$. Mass monotonicity would then imply
\[
                         2=M_\theta(W)\leq M_\theta(P)=2(1-s)<2,
\]
a contradiction. No identity asserting that envelopes commute
with maxima was used.
\end{proof}

Bernoulli measure on binary choices defines a probability μ_0 supported on C, giving each level-n interval mass 2^-n. The nested interval lengths tend to zero, so each binary choice has a unique limit point. For any point the mass of its singleton is at most 2^-n for every n, hence zero. Define D=C+2, μ_1 the translate of μ_0. C and D are disjoint compact sets, both avoiding infinity.

For finite t use the spherical kernel

    G_t(z)=log(|z−t|²/((1+|z|²)(1+|t|²)))≤0,
    dd^c G_t=δ_t−ω_z,
    U_j(z)=∫G_t(z)dμ_j(t).

The identity for G_t follows from dd^c log|z−t|²=δ_t and dd^c log(1+|z|²)=ω_z, and extends at infinity by the affine coordinate 1/z. For example, choose a=1/2, s=1/2. Both ideal families are O_X(-floor(c/2)E); both first-degree products are (1/2)π*ω_z+π*ω_w; both top measures equal π*(ω_z∧ω_w), of raw mass 1. Their normalized P-envelopes differ. The ambient intersection α²=7/4 does not equal that raw mass.

## Consequences and exact limitations

For a fixed s∈(0,1), the data ((I(cu))_{c>0},<T_u>,<T_u²>) of the two examples agree but their P-envelopes do not. Any proposed reconstruction map with precisely that input therefore fails. In particular, ideal data plus a scalar raw mass are insufficient. Varying s in one family proves that ideal data alone cannot recover raw mass or raw top measure, even in this actual big non-nef class.

This says nothing about sufficiently rich birational, movable, or additional singularity data. We do not claim that a full system of such data coincides for the two examples. We do not construct a non-Archimedean metric, positivity cone, compatible DXZ family, or MP comparison. The all-point ideal formula is not a general all-semivaluation reconstruction formula for the active P14.8 task.

The varying-mass mechanism is an extension of the known ample-curve obstruction already in the supplied catalogue, not a new full target result. The same-mass separation provides a further concrete test for a data proposal. P14.4 stays open as a construction problem. The measures here are complex BEGZ measures, so P14.5 stays open as a non-Archimedean realization and comparison problem. No energy or E¹ identification is established, so P14.6 stays open. P14.1's intrinsic image outside its known scopes is untouched. At s=1 the class is still big but the potential has zero raw mass; this supplies no filtration interval, arbitrary-formal-data realization, or canonical new reconstruction for P14.8.
